title: Publish WinGet and Scoop channels
notes: This tree already carried a prior, incomplete pass at this task (commit 199d790f, 'feat(distribution): add Windows channel source contract'): packaging/winget/release.v1.json, packaging/scoop/membrane.json, scripts/release/verify-windows-channels.mjs, and tests/platform/windows/package-channels.test.mjs. That pass built an internal JSON binding contract for both channels (fail-closed, publish:false, state unavailable/ready) but never produced the actual installable manifest formats WinGet and Scoop each need, and left sourceIdentity/artifact/channels null with no defined derivation path. This task's additions are strictly additive on top of it: none of those four pre-existing files were modified (verified by re-running the pre-existing tests/platform/windows/package-channels.test.mjs unchanged; see commands.log).

Mid-task correction from the orchestrator: RightKit (tools/rightkit/packages/release/) already owns Windows signing and is already wired into apps/membrane-hub (right-release.config.mjs's targets.win: src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/Membrane_<version>_x64-setup.exe, sign.files, installer key membrane/installers/windows/current/Membrane_x64-setup.exe, updater block; package.json's release:build:win runs `right-release build --platform win`). The channel manifests must consume RightKit's actual sealed release output, not a parallel notion of a release. scripts/release/channels/right-release-source.mjs reads & independently re-verifies RightKit's sealed .right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<commit8>/windows/release-manifest.json (schema 1, checkpoints through 'sealed', on-disk file hash/size for every listed artifact -- the same integrity proof tools/rightkit/packages/release/release-state.mjs#verifySealedRelease requires, reimplemented as a same-repo JSON reader rather than importing RightKit's package, per tools/rightkit's own 'apps consume published versions, never parent paths' rule) and derives {version, commit, installerName, installerSha256, installerUrl} from it. installerUrl reuses the exact PUBLIC_DOWNLOAD_BASE constant (https://pub-6c73208d46c245a9b4881d5e02f6b618.r2.dev, overridable by the same RIGHTAPPS_PUBLIC_DOWNLOAD_BASE env var) tools/rightkit/packages/release/pub-upload.mjs already uses to verify uploaded artifacts, combined with the sealed manifest's own routes.patch[] installer key -- never an invented URL.

The artifact is x64-only today (right-release.config.mjs defines exactly one Windows target). deriveWindowsChannelArtifact in right-release-source.mjs treats any sealed manifest with more than one installer-role file, or one whose name is not the x64 NSIS pattern, as a declared, validated gap -- it throws a named 'declared gap' error rather than guessing an architecture or silently picking one (test: 'deriveWindowsChannelArtifact declares a gap instead of guessing on multiple or non-x64 installers').

scripts/release/channels/generate-windows-channels.mjs combines that real RightKit-sourced artifact with a validated MBR-902 clean-machine receipt, reusing scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs#validateReceipt and scripts/release/verify-windows-channels.mjs#verifyWindowsChannels completely unmodified (both files are outside this task's allowlist; both are imported read-only). It builds the ready-state packaging/winget/release.v1.json contract shape those unmodified validators already enforce, and produces & validates the real WinGet + Scoop manifests before writeGeneratedChannels ever touches disk. When either the sealed release or the receipt is missing/invalid, it returns status 'unavailable' with named reasons and writes nothing -- proven directly against the live repo root by the test 'today's real membrane checkout has no sealed Windows release: nothing is invented', which asserts loadWindowsChannelArtifact returns null for this actual checkout (only mac releases exist under .right-release/sealed/ today).

scripts/release/channels/winget-manifest.mjs builds the real, installable WinGet multi-file manifest (version/installer/defaultLocale YAML, PackageIdentifier Orthic.Membrane) that was missing before this task: InstallerType nsis, Architecture x64, InstallerSwitches {Silent: '/S', SilentWithProgress: '/S'} for silent install, UpgradeBehavior 'install' for installed-version upgrade detection. No YAML package is installed in this workspace (checked: absent from package.json and node_modules) and installing one is out of scope, so renderWingetYaml is a small hand-rolled, narrowly-scoped emitter (JSON-quoted scalars, no escaping logic) rather than a general YAML library -- declared under MINIMIZE as MIN_CUSTOM after NOT_BUILD/REUSE/STDLIB/NATIVE/INSTALLED_DEP/ONE_LINE were rejected for the reasons above.

scripts/release/channels/scoop-manifest.mjs adds the real installable fields Scoop's already-real single-JSON format was missing: architecture.64bit.installer/uninstaller (both '/S'), plus checkver/autoupdate for version-detected upgrade. unavailableScoopManifest() is asserted byte-identical to the pre-existing, unmodified packaging/scoop/membrane.json.

packaging/winget/manifests/o/Orthic/Membrane/UNAVAILABLE/*.yaml holds the intentionally-invalid placeholder trio for today's true state (no sealed Windows release exists): PackageVersion '0.0.0-unavailable' (fails the strict-SemVer check), InstallerUrl/InstallerSha256 explicit 'UNAVAILABLE: ...' sentinels (fail the https-URL / 64-hex-SHA-256 checks) -- validateWingetManifests rejects this trio by design (asserted by test), mirroring packaging/homebrew/Casks/membrane.rb's fail-closed `raise` for WinGet's declarative format. These files are byte-identical to renderWingetYaml(unavailableWingetManifests()...) (asserted by test), so they cannot silently drift from the generator that would replace them.

The acceptance criterion 'winget and scoop install/upgrade/uninstall pass on clean Windows' is demonstrated as a deterministic, fail-closed generator/validator pipeline sourced from RightKit's real signed artifact: buildWingetManifests/buildScoopManifest refuse a non-ready contract; validateWingetManifests/validateScoopManifest require real https URLs, real 64-hex SHA-256, silent /S install AND uninstall flags on both channels, and version-detection fields (WinGet UpgradeBehavior: install; Scoop checkver/autoupdate) before accepting a manifest as installable. Actually running `winget install`/`winget upgrade`/`winget uninstall` and `scoop install`/`scoop update`/`scoop uninstall` on a clean Windows machine requires a real sealed & uploaded RightKit release plus the MBR-902/MBR-806 clean-machine receipts, which this task's hard rules and stop conditions reserve for the Book 3 final phased gate (MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md) -- this task ships only the generator/validator pipeline that lets that later run be proven deterministically from RightKit's real output, not the run itself.

Every field a real artifact would need -- version, URL, SHA-256 -- is either copied verbatim from an independently-re-verified RightKit sealed manifest (in the 'ready' path, exercised only against synthetic test fixtures, never against this checkout's real, still-empty .right-release/sealed/ tree) or is a declared, validation-rejecting placeholder (in the committed 'unavailable' path). No version, URL, or SHA-256 was invented anywhere in this change.
No cargo build/test, no pnpm/Tauri build, no right-release/winget/scoop/signtool invocation, and no mutating git command was run at any point in this task.
